data.title: PR-22 IMPL-09: receipt policy decision recomputed from the IMPL-06 verdict for the named version; claims refused on disagreement; promotion licensed only when PromoteEligible

data.body: [HIGH] Same-version cached verdicts can issue a promotion license without current recomputation. ReceiptDecision::derive accepts any public PolicyVerdicts provider, then only checks the returned verdict against the transaction handle and identity at lines 301-306. Classification and evidence freshness are not bound. The added regression at crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr22_impl09_policy_decision.rs:496-500 proves that a held verdict remains accepted for its own version. A provider can therefore return an earlier PromoteEligible verdict after current semantic or intent classification becomes review or block, or after current evidence becomes unavailable. The allow claim then passes crates/continuum-repair/src/receipt.rs:1502-1503 and can produce ReceiptGenerationLicense, contrary to RFC 0032 and INV-015. Failure modes: stale allow bypasses protected-intent review or unavailable-evidence refusal. Edge cases: another-version caches fail, but same identity caches and omitted classification pass. Rollback: reject this range; no production promotion path exists yet. Monitoring: assert and audit that every promotion recomputes classification and evidence and never accepts a cached provider result. Validation: add one same-transaction test where an earlier allow is followed by current review, block, or unavailable evidence; the held result must be refused and no license returned. Fix: close or seal PolicyVerdicts, or make verification invoke PolicyVerdict::compute directly from current GateReasons plus the mandatory promotion-time classification and evidence. Transaction identity alone is not freshness.

data.reason: HIGH: ReceiptDecision accepts a cached same-version PromoteEligible verdict, so promotion can bypass the required current semantic and intent classification recomputation.
